instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Commands_System is explicitly the User Command SSOT while adjacent runtime, provider, storage, routing, widget, and GUI contracts remain owner-projected consumers rather than command-local redefinitions.
atoms.title: User Commands ownership is explicit and bounded

atoms.statement: The source clearly distinguishes user-authored content presets from developer-defined dispatch IDs and names cmd.chat.run_user_command as the bridge instead of making each preset a UICommand.
atoms.title: User Commands and UICommands are not conflated

atoms.statement: The canonical example and preservation criteria use persona, mode, model, and subtask, while the field contract uses persona_override, mode_override, and model_override and omits subtask; the example also omits the required name field. A parser, serializer, GUI, and migration cannot infer whether aliases are accepted, rejected, or normalized.
atoms.title: Frontmatter has mutually incompatible canonical field sets

atoms.statement: Arguments are substituted before include and shell scans, and included file text is inserted before shell injection. The contract never says whether syntax introduced by an argument or included file is inert data or is reparsed as @path or !`command`; it also defines no literal escaping syntax.
atoms.title: Sequential template expansion does not define token inertness

atoms.statement: The include contract does not define the base directory for relative paths, canonicalization before permission matching, traversal and symlink handling, TOCTOU behavior, binary/encoding failures, deterministic directory ordering, recursion, entry/byte limits, cancellation, or redaction of sensitive paths.
atoms.title: File include resolution lacks containment, determinism, and resource limits

atoms.statement: Beyond permission gating and stdout insertion, shell execution has no specified shell/interpreter, environment, cwd binding verification, timeout, cancellation, output cap, encoding, stderr or exit-status behavior, partial-output rule, secret redaction, process-tree cleanup, or audit correlation.
atoms.title: Shell injection has no execution or failure envelope

atoms.statement: Child work is required to inherit and narrow the parent permission ceiling, but permissions_profile_override effectively replaces the Persona profile. The command contract does not state that the replacement is intersected with the parent ceiling or what happens when the profile is missing, malformed, changed during execution, or attempts to widen authority.
atoms.title: Permission profile replacement is not explicitly intersected with the parent ceiling

atoms.statement: Preview promises no run submission but explicitly executes shell commands. Permission approval does not make arbitrary shell execution side-effect-free, and the UI contract provides no stronger warning, separate consent, sandbox, read-only restriction, cancellation, or side-effect result state.
atoms.title: Preview is labeled dry-run while executing real shell side effects

atoms.statement: The section declares one canonical locked set without /goal, then later lists /goal and /goal again as reserved built-ins. It also labels two different sections as section 7, so anchors and consumers cannot determine the authoritative set or target.
atoms.title: The locked reserved-command set contradicts its own Goal entries

atoms.statement: Catalog lifecycle is numbered 6.6 before 6.1, and 6.3 Shortcut binding has no body before section 7 begins. The visible shortcut surface is elsewhere called optional, but binding conflicts, scope, disabled states, platform key differences, and invocation feedback are unspecified.
atoms.title: GUI section ordering leaves shortcut behavior structurally undefined

atoms.statement: The second prologue continuation specifies child-run resolution, permission approvals, management UI, preview, reserved slash behavior, UICommand dispatch, OpenCode deltas, and AC-CMD01 through AC-CMD10.
atoms.title: Core execution, permissions, GUI, reserved commands, dispatch, baseline, and acceptance surfaces are enumerated

atoms.statement: The first PlanUnit group keeps Commands as the User Command owner, maps cross-owner references, defers backend/provider semantics, prevents chat lifecycle redefinition, normalizes route arguments through owner contracts, and rejects tier-era command-local runtime identity.
atoms.title: CS-002 through CS-007 preserve authority, owner deferral, chat, routing, and runtime identity boundaries

atoms.statement: Across CS-002 through CS-034, validation_surfaces repeat only plan migration and plan index validators. No declared oracle executes parser precedence, reserved-name rejection, permissions, child-run lineage, concurrent storage, GUI state, accessibility, or preview safety.
atoms.title: PlanUnit acceptance criteria have no behavioral validation oracle

atoms.statement: This group preserves widget/artifact/confirmation ownership, debug and launcher gates, User Command and UICommand distinctions, two-tier storage, and reserved-name validation.
atoms.title: CS-008 through CS-013 define owner-routed consumers and command identity rules

atoms.statement: The source permits /<command-name> or /x-<command-name>, while the GUI always shows an /x- prefix and storage resolves raw <name>.md. It never specifies whether both invocations are aliases, which form cmd.chat.run_user_command receives, how reserved collisions apply after normalization, or whether names beginning x- are double-prefixed.
atoms.title: Stored names, /name, and /x-name have no canonical mapping

atoms.statement: The global root is fixed to ~/.config without specifying supported-platform mapping, XDG overrides, unavailable or read-only homes, case-folding and Unicode normalization, duplicate physical files through symlinks, watcher refresh, malformed-file quarantine, or atomic discovery snapshots.
atoms.title: Discovery portability and filesystem identity are unresolved

atoms.statement: This group defines frontmatter and template behaviors, read/bash approval gates, worktree-root execution, thread-derived worktree names, relative file cards, and terminal cwd snapshots.
atoms.title: CS-014 through CS-019 specify file format, expansion, permission gates, cwd, and worktree display

atoms.statement: short_id derivation and collision domain are unspecified, numeric suffix allocation has no atomic reservation rule, and an existing directory is treated as stale without ownership validation. Missing/deleted worktrees, symlink escape, concurrent creators, cwd_snapshot invalidation, and cleanup/rollback have no state transitions.
atoms.title: Worktree identity and suffix allocation are race-prone and not recoverable

atoms.statement: This group models delegated child runs, Persona and requested/effective resolution, visible working-set retention, deterministic expansion order, profile precedence, and catalog install/update/removal behavior.
atoms.title: CS-020 through CS-026 define child-run, override, working-set, expansion, permission-profile, and catalog states

atoms.statement: The safer default is required unless advisory is declared, but the schema has no dependency/advisory field. The contract also omits parent or user cancellation propagation, child timeout, dispatch rejection, event-written/storage-failed and storage-written/dispatch-failed cases, retry/idempotency keys, orphan reconciliation, and required-child failure propagation.
atoms.title: Child-run lifecycle omits declaration, cancellation, and partial-creation behavior

atoms.statement: The UI must show effective results after policy, availability, compatibility, or account changes, while explicit requests must not silently fallback. The source does not define which changes are permitted remaps versus terminal rejection, their state/event taxonomy, whether the user can approve a remap, or how unavailable inherited defaults differ from explicit overrides.
atoms.title: Policy remap and forbidden silent fallback are not distinguished

atoms.statement: latest active result, supports the next intended action, carried forward, supersedes the same purpose, and execution clearly moves are not defined or ordered. The contract does not resolve pinned items when branches change, multi-window focus, concurrent results, retention across restart, eviction, or who authoritatively marks carry-forward.
atoms.title: Working-set membership predicates are not deterministic

atoms.statement: The source requires safe updates and deferred removal but does not define catalog identity/version/signature, provenance persistence, merge/conflict behavior with manual edits, atomic writes, interrupted install/update, offline or stale-catalog behavior, concurrent editors, deferral states and retry triggers, rollback, or what counts as an intentional user override.
atoms.title: Catalog lifecycle lacks provenance, trust, concurrency, and rollback contracts

atoms.statement: This group specifies Settings placement, provenance labels, scope selection, the command table, create/edit/delete flows, inline validation, and rendered preview.
atoms.title: CS-027 through CS-034 define the management GUI through preview rendering

atoms.statement: The table lists all project and global commands and sorts a project override before the matching global row, even though resolution makes only the project row effective. No disabled/shadowed state, effective-source marker, invocation target, scope-filter interaction, or behavior after live filesystem changes is defined.
atoms.title: The resolved-command table does not define effective versus shadowed rows

atoms.statement: Pre-populated editing and save-time validation do not bind a file revision, revalidate after external changes, reserve the name, perform an atomic durable write, or define write/rename/fsync failure and rollback. Save-as-override and save-global can race another editor, catalog update, or watcher refresh.
atoms.title: Edit and save have no optimistic concurrency or atomic commit contract

atoms.statement: Delete specifies only a generic modal and reveal behavior. It does not identify the exact scope/provenance/path and resulting effective command, reconcile catalog deferral and active references, require typed or severity-scaled confirmation, define filesystem failure/partial deletion, offer undo/trash, or record an audit event.
atoms.title: Delete confirmation has no dependency summary, failure state, or recovery

atoms.statement: The normative table, toggle, editor, modal, checkbox icon, syntax highlighting, truncation, and read-only preview specify no keyboard order/shortcuts, focus restoration, accessible names and states, screen-reader error association, non-color syntax cues, reduced motion, high contrast, zoom/reflow, long localized text, bidi/path handling, or locale-stable sorting.

atoms.statement: The source defines user copy such as Unknown command and inline validation errors but no stable error codes, source location/range, parse/include/shell/child correlation IDs, provenance snapshot, structured logs, support export, redaction policy, retryability classification, or aggregation rules for multiple failures.

atoms.statement: CS-035 prohibits run execution and agent submission but explicitly permits shell execution without specifying isolation or recovery semantics for shell side effects.

atoms.statement: CS-036 explicitly limits the 6.3 heading to source lineage and defers shortcut behavior to its owning contracts.

atoms.statement: CS-038 requires normalization and usage on parse failure but does not define accepted URL forms, unsafe targets, canonical output, or offline/transport failure behavior.

atoms.statement: ConcernRecord is explicitly distinct from findings and blocked episodes, preserves stable identity across ownership changes, and closes its primary lifecycle and resolution vocabularies.
atoms.title: Canonical concern lifecycle is materially specified

atoms.statement: The EventRecord envelope is closed and versioned, separates event_type from the legacy type alias, requires ordering and idempotency fields, forbids raw secrets, and makes migration forward-only.
atoms.title: EventRecord persistence boundary is explicit

atoms.statement: CV-292 defines a route-specific support evidence envelope and a falsifiable local-output threshold for green support, including explicit Antigravity public-catalog versus internal-image proof separation.
atoms.title: Provider support requires output-level route proof

atoms.statement: CV-292 names support and verification states plus proof_timestamp, but it does not define transition triggers, proof expiry, refresh cadence, or the failure/recovery rule that demotes previously verified support.
atoms.title: Support-proof freshness lifecycle is not closed

atoms.statement: CV-293 requires requested and effective provider, account, model, auth, transport, effort, media-route, and capability identity to remain separately queryable across consumers.
atoms.title: Requested/effective provider identity propagates across consumers

atoms.statement: The effort outcomes are enumerated semantically, but the envelope does not name the canonical outcome field, define provider-specific mapping evidence, or give discriminating oracles for skipped versus unsupported and clamped versus partially supported.
atoms.title: Thinking-effort outcome encoding remains discretionary

atoms.statement: CV-294 establishes caller-scoped capability evaluation and reference-first provider-native artifact handling under PM permission custody.
atoms.title: Provider capability is caller-scoped and permission-mediated

atoms.statement: The caller-scoped artifact contract explicitly prohibits secret and full-payload storage and uses references or bounded previews for sensitive and verbose evidence.
atoms.title: Provider and browser evidence is reference-first

atoms.statement: The same question lifecycle declares expired as the timeout outcome and then declares timed_out in the exact runtime status enum without defining a canonical normalization direction or layer boundary.
atoms.title: Question timeout state is internally inconsistent

atoms.statement: The contract requires parent and per-URL child audit events while forbidding a parallel web event family, but it does not specify child event_type, parent/correlation fields, aggregate-state algorithm, or mixed success/denial/failure behavior.
atoms.title: Batch web partial-failure event semantics are incomplete

atoms.statement: The web taxonomy maps HTTP 402 directly to rate_limited and provides no discriminator that preserves payment, quota, entitlement, retryability, or user-action semantics.
atoms.title: HTTP 402 loses billing recovery semantics

atoms.statement: AuthState conditions account and billing fields on the selected subject and quota model, and uses stable account or connection-profile IDs for identity-sensitive storage.
atoms.title: Auth subject shape avoids null-padding and display-name identity

atoms.statement: AuthState closes availability_state without eligible_pending_recheck, while the later canonical implementation enum adds that value and lifecycle rules depend on it.
atoms.title: AvailabilityState has two incompatible closed enums

atoms.statement: Check-before-use requires proactive refresh and serializes one OAuth write path, but it does not define single-flight locking, winner selection, failed-refresh rollback, concurrent waiter behavior, or whether 20% is measured against original lifetime or dynamically remaining lifetime.
atoms.title: Proactive credential refresh is race-prone

atoms.statement: Explicit and automatic auth selection are bounded by provider, role, account policy, and supported auth surface, with silent cross-provider fallback prohibited.
atoms.title: Auth resolution preserves provider and account-family boundaries

atoms.statement: HITL approvals bind to blocked-episode identity, survive restart by rehydration, and retain failed approval or recovery-action attempts as durable history.
atoms.title: Blocked-episode recovery preserves identity and failed history

atoms.statement: The canonical registrations give Remove Worktree and Merge Worktree only the shared repository/thread guard plus activeThreadHasWorktree, without specifying dirty-worktree checks, safe-point or backup requirements, confirmation, rollback, or conflict-state disablement.
atoms.title: Destructive worktree commands lack safety gates

atoms.statement: route_target closes destination classes, selectors, object kinds, focus refinements, resolver scope, disposition, rejection, and compatibility normalization while prohibiting escape-hatch arguments.
atoms.title: Canonical route identity is closed and validated

atoms.statement: The route contract validates field combinations but does not specify trust classification, authorization revalidation, account/tenant binding, replay expiry, or safe handling for untrusted serialized resume_url inputs, especially at global resolver scope.
atoms.title: Serialized routes lack an authority and trust boundary

atoms.statement: Account-sensitive panel/cache state is partitioned or invalidated, and blocked privileged work revalidates its requested identity before resume.
atoms.title: Account switches invalidate state and reauthorize queued work

atoms.statement: Resend is explicitly destructive, but the contract does not specify confirmation thresholds, affected-history preview, preservation or branching, rollback, undo, or audit behavior.
atoms.title: Resend discards history without a safety contract

atoms.statement: Every token bucket must be present or explicitly unknown/not_exposed, but the canonical field type and serialization that distinguishes numeric zero, unknown, and not_exposed are not defined.
atoms.title: Unknown token buckets have no canonical wire shape

atoms.statement: The cost contract requires unsigned persisted microdollars and monotonic totals, yet permits negative-cost display backed by an adjustment record without defining a signed adjustment amount type or projection algorithm.
atoms.title: Negative adjustments have no representable canonical amount

atoms.statement: Usage attribution is keyed by a canonical provider/model/account/billing/entitlement tuple and preserves parent_run_id for helper and child work rather than creating a second usage model.
atoms.title: Usage attribution preserves account and child-run lineage

atoms.statement: The scale range and Slint mechanism are fixed, but the contract does not define composition with platform scale, per-monitor changes, keyboard/accessibility operation, persistence scope, or how users select non-preset values up to 1.5.
atoms.title: UI scaling lacks accessibility and multi-display semantics
